disposition_reason: In vitro pharmacology of the organic gallium complex KP46 in human osteosarcoma lines and non-malignant fibroblasts; cytotoxicity IC50 values only, no gallium measured in any food, water, environmental or human matrix.

study.design: in vitro cell-line cytotoxicity and mechanism study
study.method: MTT viability (72 h), clonogenic assay (7 d), flow cytometry, migration assays

regulatory_or_exposure: KP46 IC50 (72 h MTT) 1.204 to 3.830 µM in four human osteosarcoma lines; 9.01 µM in non-malignant human lung fibroblasts (Table 1, p. 6)
non_numeric_findings: Gallium compounds are described as acting mainly by competing with iron uptake and inhibiting the iron-dependent enzyme ribonucleotide reductase (Background, p. 2; secondary)
Simple gallium salts (nitrate, chloride) were evaluated clinically but unfavorable pharmacokinetic and toxicological properties prevented routine use (Background, p. 2; secondary)
KP46 reached a phase-I clinical trial in renal cell cancer (Background, p. 2; secondary)
